item.title: Thanos
item.description:
Thanos runbook#

This page is for you if you operate the Thanos metrics store that materialize-monitoring installs, and one of its components has stopped working. Each section starts from an alert or an error you can see, and ends when the component is healthy again. For a symptom that no section here matches, see o11y Troubleshooting.

Thanos Compactor#

The Thanos Compactor merges the blocks that Receive uploads into larger ones, downsamples them, and deletes blocks that are past retention. It runs as a single replica, thanos-compactor-0, and works from the bucket. Nothing on its volume is authoritative, so a Compactor that loses its volume redoes the work and loses no data.

item.title: Kubernetes
item.description:
Kubernetes runbook#

This page is for you if you operate the Kubernetes cluster that materialize-monitoring runs on. It holds the procedures that apply to more than one component. The component runbooks link here for those steps.

Storage#

These procedures change the PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) that the stack’s StatefulSets create from their volumeClaimTemplates.

Temporarily increase storage of working PVCs#

A working PVC holds only a cache or a scratch copy of data that lives elsewhere, usually the bucket. Losing one costs the component time to rebuild it, and loses no data. A one-off job, such as the Thanos Compactor’s first run after a long halt, can need more space than the component needs in steady state. You can grow a working PVC for that job, and later return it to the chart’s size.
